title: Stale Time & Garbage Collection
description: Understand stale time and garbage collection in React Query to manage cache lifecycle effectively.

data.text: Stale time determines how long React Query considers data fresh. While data is fresh, React Query will not refetch it in the background. Once stale, the next consumer triggers a background refetch. Setting staleTime to Infinity makes data never stale, turning React Query into a client-side cache with no automatic updates.

data.title: Infinite stale time example
data.content: Use Infinity for truly static reference data.

data.text: When a query is no longer observed by any component, it enters the garbage collection timer. If no component subscribes before `cacheTime` expires, the query is removed from cache. This frees memory but means the next mount will show a loading state.

data.definition:
graph TD
    A[Query Active] --> B[All Components Unmount]
    B --> C[GC Timer Starts]
    C --> D{ cacheTime Expired? }
    D -->|No| E[Query Remains in Cache]
    D -->|Yes| F[Query Removed]
    E --> G[Component Remounts]
    G --> H[Instant Data from Cache]
    F --> I[Component Remounts]
    I --> J[Loading State + Refetch]
data.caption: Garbage collection flow

items: Use staleTime: 0 for real-time or frequently changing data.
Use staleTime: Infinity for static reference data.
Set cacheTime between 5-30 minutes for most applications.
Increase cacheTime for expensive queries that users revisit often.
data.title: Guidelines

data.text: Garbage collection only runs for unused queries. Active queries are never collected. This means you can safely use long cacheTimes for queries that are frequently accessed.
data.title: GC Safety
Stale Time & GC Key Points
points: staleTime controls when data is considered outdated.
Garbage collection removes unused queries after cacheTime.
Active queries are never garbage collected.
data.takeaway: Understanding stale time and garbage collection lets you tune React Query for both performance and memory efficiency.
